CLARANS on a shape distance matrix

Source: R/shape_medoid3d.R
shape_clarans.Rd

Clustering Large Applications based on RANdomized Search (Ng and Han, 2002), in the faster variant of Schubert and Rousseeuw (2021): random restarts of a randomized medoid-swap search. Own implementation in C++ that uses R's random-number stream.

Usage

shape_clarans(
  D,
  K,
  numlocal = 2L,
  maxneighbor = 0.0125,
  distance = c("rho", "dF", "dP"),
  reflection = FALSE
)

Arguments

D

Numeric \(n \times n\) distance matrix, or a real landmark array \(k \times m \times n\), or a complex pre-shape matrix, from which distances are computed with distance.

K

Number of clusters (>= 2).

numlocal

Number of random restarts (default 2).

maxneighbor

Search effort of each restart. A value below 1 is a rate and means r = ceiling(maxneighbor * (n - K)); a value of 1 or more is taken as r itself. A restart ends after r - 1 consecutive unsuccessful swap trials, so r = 1 tries no swap at all. Default 0.0125.

distance

Distance used if D is not a distance matrix: one of "rho" (default), "dF", "dP".

reflection

Passed to shape_distance when D is a landmark array.

Value

A list with components:

cluster

Integer vector of length n, values in 1:K: the index of the nearest medoid.

medoids

Integer vector of length K, 1-based object indices.

objective

Sum of the distances of the objects to their medoid.

n_iter

Number of accepted swaps in the restart that gave the returned medoids.

distance

Distance name, or NA if D was a distance matrix.

Details

A restart draws K distinct random medoids. It then repeatedly draws a random non-medoid \(h\), evaluates the change of the total cost for swapping \(h\) with each of the K medoids at once, and performs the best swap if it lowers the cost; the restart ends after \(r - 1\) consecutive trials without a swap, with \(r\) defined at maxneighbor. The best restart is returned. The defaults are those of the 3D bagging scripts, which called fastkmedoids::fastclarans() with numlocal = 2 and maxneighbor = 0.0125. This function follows the same algorithm but draws from R's generator, so for the same set.seed() it does not return the partition of that package, and nothing beyond base R is needed.

With the default maxneighbor, \(r = 1\) whenever \(n - K \le 80\), so no swap is ever tried and the result is the better of numlocal random medoid sets; for \(n = 100\) and \(K = 2\) (\(r = 2\)) one failed trial ends a restart. Raise maxneighbor (for instance to 0.3, or to a count such as 100) for a real search.

References

Ng, R. T. and Han, J. (2002). CLARANS: a method for clustering objects for spatial data mining. IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering, 14(5), 1003–1016. doi:10.1109/TKDE.2002.1033770

Schubert, E. and Rousseeuw, P. J. (2021). Fast and eager k-medoids clustering: O(k) runtime improvement of the PAM, CLARA, and CLARANS algorithms. Information Systems, 101, 101804. doi:10.1016/j.is.2021.101804

See also

shape_pam, shape_hill, bagclust1

Examples

sim <- sim_shapes3d(n = 10, sigma = 0.5, seed = 1)
D <- shape_distance(sim$X)
set.seed(1)
fit <- shape_clarans(D, K = 2)
table(fit$cluster, sim$group)
#>    
#>     1 2
#>   1 7 1
#>   2 3 9
